targets.authors: Watson Todd, R. and Pojanapunya. P.
targets.title: Implicit attitudes towards native and non-native speaker teachers.
targets.evidence_quote:
The purpose of this study, then, is to replicate Watson Todd and Pojanapunya (2009) to see
if changes in the sociolinguistic context have influenced attitudes towards NESTs and LETs in
Thailand.
targets.outcome_quote:
From Table 3, we can see that the previous explicit preference for NESTs has remained
unchanged, the previous warmer feelings towards LETs have now become neutral, and the previous
lack of any implicit preference has now become a weak implicit preference for NESTs. Overall, it
appears that there has been a shift in attitudes of all types in favour of NESTs.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly retain the original explicit preference for NESTs but contrast the original warmer feelings towards LETs and absent implicit preference with new neutral feelings and weak implicit NEST preference. These are partial agreement and partial disagreement with the published findings. Failure of their new temporal-change expectation is not itself a replication outcome.

reasoning: Same instrument and analysis procedures, new comparable Thai university sample. One original paper is explicitly retested; references to IAT methods and other attitude studies are contextual.
